In March this year, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro and confirmed it has no intention of releasing any new Mac Pro hardware.

Bloomberg's latest report published today further reveals the full story behind Apple's Mac Pro strategy, including one unexpected detail involving a product Apple once developed...

The Inside Story of Apple Shelving Mac Pro Plans

In the latest edition of his "Power On" newsletter, Mark Gurman explains that discontinuing the Mac Pro "was not always the planned outcome." He reiterates a key point from earlier reports: Apple had originally planned to release a processor positioned above its "Ultra" chip, codenamed "Extreme."

The report states: "Apple is understood to have developed both the M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme chips, but ultimately shelved the projects based on considerations of cost and demand."

As for the specific Mac Pro hardware under development, Gurman indicates that Apple internally had two models (codenamed J170 and J190), but neither was ever officially announced.

The most striking detail in the report is that one of the models used an Intel processor:

Apple officially discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its official website, and directed buyers to purchase the Mac Studio instead. This ending actually showed signs from early on, but for Mac Pro hardware enthusiasts, it still marks the end of an era and is inevitably a cause for regret.

What are your thoughts on Apple's decision to discontinue the entire Mac Pro product line in the Apple Silicon era rather than continuing to release "Extreme" chips? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
